subject: Computer Networking
title: Zigbee and Smart Homes
description: A quick win: understand Zigbee and Smart Homes.

hook.text: Your smart light, thermostat, and door lock talk to each other. They don't use Wi-Fi — they use Zigbee.

buildup.text: Zigbee is a low-power, low-data-rate protocol. It forms a mesh where devices relay messages for each other.

discovery.text: Each Zigbee device can act as a router. The mesh self-heals — remove one node and traffic reroutes automatically.

twist.text: The new Matter standard builds on Zigbee's mesh ideas but adds interoperability across brands and protocols.

climax.text: Zigbee runs on coin-cell batteries for years. Wi-Fi drains batteries in days. For sensors, that gap is huge.

punchline.text: Zigbee proves that low power and slow speed can be a strength.

quiz.question: Why is Zigbee preferred over Wi-Fi for smart home sensors?
options: It uses much less power, allowing batteries to last years
It has a longer range than Wi-Fi

details.summary: Zigbee is a low-power wireless mesh protocol designed for smart home devices like lights, locks, sensors, and thermostats. Devices relay messages through each other to extend range.
details.whyItMatters: Zigbee and its successor Matter are foundational to smart home ecosystems. Understanding mesh IoT protocols explains how homes become intelligent networks of interconnected devices.
takeaways: Zigbee creates a self-healing mesh network of smart home devices
Battery-powered sensors operate for years on low power
Matter standard builds on Zigbee concepts for cross-vendor compatibility

faq.question: How does Zigbee compare to Wi-Fi for smart home devices?
faq.answer: Zigbee uses far less power, enabling battery-operated devices that last years. It supports thousands of devices per network versus Wi-Fi's hundreds. Zigbee's mesh topology provides better coverage. However, Zigbee requires a dedicated hub and has much lower data rates.

faq.question: What is the Matter smart home standard?
faq.answer: Matter is a new industry standard backed by Apple, Google, Amazon, and Samsung that provides cross-vendor smart home interoperability. It runs over Wi-Fi and Thread, a protocol similar to Zigbee. Matter devices work with any compatible platform, ending the fragmentation of competing ecosystems.
